In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the outermost parts of SNe Ia are almost spherical, the outermost parts and the innermost parts of S-type SNe II are almost spherical, while the inner parts of S-type and I-type SNe II and the inner parts of all SNe Ib are highly aspherical.
core-collapse supernovas are highly asymmetric, and this is the case for the majority of them, including SNe IIP, SNe IIL, SNe Ib, SNe Ic, and SNe Ic-BL.
all core-collapse supernovas are intrinsically aspherical, but the degree to which the outer parts of their ejecta are aspherical is not yet clear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found that the core of SN 2008ax was very spherical, but that the core of the other three SNe were not.
we have shown that the innermost layers in SNe IIP have large asphericities, and we have shown that this is true for a large fraction of SNe IIn as well (see also our companion paper).
the outer layers are largely spherical, while the inner layers of core-collapse supernova ejecta are highly asymmetric.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ejecta of ordinary SNe IIP have a high degree of asphericities, which is consistent with the idea that these explosions are powered by the collapse of an aspherical core.
the asphericities of core-collapse supernova ejecta are not limited to a small fraction of events, but are instead ubiquitous, even in the case of SNe I IP.
the asphericity is present in the innermost parts of the ejectas and that the degree of asphericty in SNe IIP increases toward the core, with the innermost parts being the most aspherical.
